newsitem.title: USA: Conn. voters okay a number of large bond issues.
newsitem.headline: Conn. voters okay a number of large bond issues.

text.p: Connecticut's voters approved a number of larger bond issues on the November 5 ballot, according to unofficial results provided by local officials. A list of some of the larger initiatives follows.

Approved appropriations aggregating $14.9 million for various public improvements and authorizing the issuance of $14.9 million of bonds to meet such appropriations, and pending issuance, the making of temporary borrowings. --Hartford: winning margin of 13,644 versus 1,960 against. Approved an ordinance authorizing $20 million of bonds for improvements to certain schools be approved;

Winning margin of 13,111 versus 1,903 against. Approved ordinances authorizing the issuance of a total of $13.7 million of city bonds for planning, acquisition, construction, reconstruction and renovation of 5 schools throughout the city;
Approved an ordinance authorizing $16 million of bonds for renovations and improvements to Hartford public libraries, central library and 3 branches.

--Middletown: winning margin of 7,655 versus 5,382 against. Approved bond ordinance and appropriations for $9.96 million for the acquisition of land and for the planning, acquisition and construction of a new police headquarters. --Montvale: winning margin of 2,505 versus 1,627 against. Approved $2.5 million be appropriated and bonds authorized for
the expansion and modification of the Montvale Sewage

Norwich: winning margin of 5,652 versus 4,308 against. Approved $11.5 million be appropriated and bonds authorized for the expansion and renovation of Samuel Huntington and Bishop elementary schools; $11 million be appropriated and bonds authorized for the implementation of citywide schools
